components.title: FAO yield response to water
components.used_for: Relative crop yield response to evapotranspiration deficit. Period yields and severe-deficit cutoff remain explicit Harvest assumptions.

components.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56
components.used_for: Extraterrestrial radiation and reference evaporation framework. Hargreaves demand uses the atlas day/night range.

components.title: Galor and Özak: Caloric Suitability Index
components.used_for: Caloric productivity and historically available crops as agricultural suitability. We use our own simulated climate and period yields, not the CSI raster or a reproduction of GAEZ.

components.title: Klein Goldewijk et al. 2017: HYDE 3.2
components.used_for: Distinguishing population totals from environmental allocation. HYDE requires historical population inputs; it is not our population predictor.

components.title: Lemmen 2009: Global Land Use and technological Evolution Simulator
components.used_for: Resource-limited population, technology, clearing and subsistence as distinct concepts. We do not claim to run GLUES demographic dynamics.

components.title: Mordecai et al. 2013: Optimal temperature for malaria transmission is dramatically lower than previously predicted
components.used_for: Equation 2 and Table 2: all seven thermal traits and mu=-log(daily survival). Competence percentages become probabilities. Fixed normalization gives a rounded-coefficient optimum of 25.57 C.

components.title: Ryan et al. 2015: Mapping Physiological Suitability Limits for Malaria in Africa Under Climate Change
components.used_for: Mapping relative physiological potential and seasonal duration; suitability is distinct from absolute transmission risk.

components.title: Craig, Snow and le Sueur 1999: A climate-based distribution model of malaria transmission in sub-Saharan Africa
components.used_for: Rainfall as a moisture constraint with an 80 mm/month wet limit. Our smooth rainfall gate plus irrigation is an explicit adaptation, not the full MARA algorithm.

components.title: Meshesha et al. 2019: Estimating carrying capacity and stocking rates of rangelands in Harshin District
components.used_for: Forage supply times a sustainable use fraction divided by feed requirements. Conversion from Miami NPP to accessible forage and human calories is a scenario allowance.

components.title: Colorado State University: Stocking rate and carrying capacity
components.used_for: The 25-30% forage consumption allowance; we use 25%. This is a land-health budget, not a validation of ancient livestock output.

components.title: Lieth 1975: Modeling the primary productivity of the world
components.used_for: Miami temperature/precipitation-limited net primary productivity, inherited from Harvest.

caution: Published biophysical components are combined with declared scenario assumptions. This is not a published or independently validated model of 200 AD population density.
